title: My ex bought his own hoodie back from me

hooks.text: My ex bought his own hoodie back... from me.
The buyer's name looked familiar. Too familiar.
Never keep your ex's hoodie. Sell it.

beats.text: My ex bought his own hoodie back... from *me*.
beats.visual: Tiff holds a grey hoodie up with a smug look; a phone shows SOLD.

beats.text: He left it at my place when we broke up.
beats.visual: Bedroom; the grey hoodie on top of the chair pile; Tiff looks at it, sad.

beats.text: For three months, it just lived on my *chair*.
beats.visual: Calendar pages flip; the pile grows around the hoodie.

beats.text: My best friend said burn it. I said, it's a really *nice* hoodie.
beats.visual: Best friend with a torch; Tiff hugs the hoodie protectively.

beats.text: So I listed it. Size large. Smells like *regret*.
beats.visual: Tiff snaps a photo; a listing board: GREY HOODIE, L.

beats.text: A week later, it sells. And the buyer's name looks... *familiar*.
beats.visual: Phone dings SOLD; Tiff leans in, eyes go wide.

beats.text: Then a message: hey, is this *mine*?
beats.visual: Whip to the ex's apartment: he is typing on his phone, confused.
Whip back: Tiff typing, smug wink.

beats.text: The rest of my chair? Listed everywhere at once with *pileGo*.
beats.visual: Quick plug: the chair, a pileGo! sign pops up, marketplace boards light up, the pile shrinks.
